_README: This file is managed by LazyCue (see shelley/lazycue). Do NOT edit by hand — it is the cached, machine-generated DSL for a self-healing browser test. To change behavior, edit the test description and re-run LazyCue.
description: The test seeds a 12-turn conversation at /c/{{SLUG}} whose first two user messages have data-message-id {{FIRST}} and {{SECOND}}; the URL fragments that link to them are {{FIRST_FRAGMENT}} and {{SECOND_FRAGMENT}}. window.fragmentScrolls lists the data-message-id of every element scrolled into view so far, in order; check it with an eval of JSON.stringify(window.fragmentScrolls). Call "append" sends another message and waits for its reply; after it, {{APPENDED}} is the reply's data-message-id. To "set the fragment to X", eval a promise that sets location.hash to X and resolves on the next hashchange event. "At the bottom" means the messages container (".messages-container") has scrollHeight - clientHeight - scrollTop below 5 and the scroll-to-bottom button (".scroll-to-bottom-button") is hidden. To "delay" a message, rename its data-message-id attribute to data-delayed-message-id, as if its element had not mounted yet; to "mount" it, set data-message-id back from data-delayed-message-id (leaving the other attribute). Perform the steps in order. Conversation changes resolve after loading, even with the same fragment. The page runs on a fake clock that steps advance with eval "window.__clock.runFor(ms)". There is a second seeded conversation, /c/{{SLUG2}}. The server's answer to loading it is held back until call "release", and the message in it that comes second in its transcript is given the ID {{FIRST}} as well; call "loading" says whether that load has started ("true" or "false"). 1. The very first step navigates straight to /c/{{SLUG}}#{{FIRST_FRAGMENT}}: the page loads with the fragment already in its URL (do not load the conversation first). 2. window.fragmentScrolls should become ["{{FIRST}}"]. 3. Switch the app to /c/{{SLUG2}}#{{FIRST_FRAGMENT}} the way its router would: eval history.pushState(null, "", that URL) and then dispatch a PopStateEvent("popstate") on window. 4. Call "loading" until it returns "true". 5. window.fragmentScrolls must still be exactly ["{{FIRST}}"]. 6. Call "release". 7. window.fragmentScrolls should become ["{{FIRST}}","{{FIRST}}"]. 8. Switch back to /c/{{SLUG}} (no fragment) the same pushState-and-popstate way, and wait for an element [data-message-id="{{SECOND}}"] to exist. 9. Call "append" and wait for an element with data-message-id {{APPENDED}} to exist. 10. Run the clock for 1100ms: window.fragmentScrolls must still be exactly ["{{FIRST}}","{{FIRST}}"].
